MindaNews published the book. It was one of several Diaz wrote on Mindanao, after Understanding Mindanao Conflict in 2003 and The 2010 GRP-MILF Peace Drafts, written with historian Rudy Rodil.

books.title: Fields of Hope
books.subtitle: Stories on Inter-religious Dialogue and Peace-building
books.summary: Stories from Pikit, Cotabato, where the author served as parish priest, of Muslims and Christians rebuilding trust after war. It draws on years of interfaith and peacebuilding work in a town hit hard by war.
books.overview:
This book collects stories by Fr. Roberto C. Layson, a Catholic missionary priest, from his MindaNews column of the same name. MindaNews editor Carol Arguillas suggested turning the columns into a book. Most of the stories come from Pikit, Cotabato, where he spent 10 years working on dialogue between Muslims and Christians.

Layson was a parish priest in Bongao, Jolo and Pikit from 1988 to 2008, and led his congregation's inter-religious ministry. He received the Pax Christi International Peace Award in 2002.

The stories share one message: that inter-religious dialogue and peacebuilding are not impossible, even if work at the grassroots looks small and its results take time to show.

books.title: Their War, Our Struggle
books.subtitle: Stories of Children in Central Mindanao
books.summary: Accounts from displaced children of Pikit and Carmen in Cotabato and Pagalungan in Maguindanao who lived through the 2000 and 2003 wars between the army and the MILF. It looks at how they coped and what in their families and communities helped them.
books.overview:
This 137-page study by Eddie Quitoriano and Theofeliz Marie Francisco presents the views of displaced children from Pikit and Carmen in Cotabato and Pagalungan in Maguindanao. These children lived through the wars of 2000 and 2003 between the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. Save the Children UK's Philippines programme published it in 2004.

The study looks at how the children coped, and at what in their families and communities shaped how they responded. The research was done at a time when programmes built on children's rights were still unfamiliar to most government and civil society groups in the region.

books.title: 25 Khutbah
books.summary: 25 Friday sermons written by 25 ulama from across Mindanao who trained at universities in Muslim countries. The sermons, in Arabic with an English translation, are meant as supplementary material for those who deliver the khutbah.
books.overview:
This book collects 25 Friday sermons (khutbah) written by 25 ulama from different regions of Mindanao, graduates in various fields of colleges and universities in Muslim countries. The sermons are written in Arabic, and an English translation is published with them as a companion.

The sermons are meant as extra material for those who deliver the Friday khutbah. Their main aim is to convey the true concepts and values of Islam to Friday congregations and to urge listeners, in suitable language, to keep away from extremist groups. They are arranged as 25 modules on 5 major themes, as one way of helping address violent extremism. The book was published in 2019 and runs to 227 pages.

books.title: Dar-ul Salam
books.subtitle: A Vision of Peace for Mindanao
books.summary: A photo-documentary, with photographs by Bobby Timonera, in which key actors in the Mindanao conflict each describe their vision of peace. It also shows everyday rural life in North Cotabato and Maguindanao during an uneasy ceasefire, in English and Maguindanaon.
books.overview:
This photo-documentary brings together people with key roles in the Mindanao conflict. Each one gives their own vision of peace, or Dar-ul Salam.

Alongside these accounts are pictures of daily life in the villages of North Cotabato and Maguindanao during a ceasefire. The library description calls that time unstable but full of hope, after a civil conflict then 41 years old. Pressia Arifin-Cabo, Joel Dizon and Khomenie Mantawel wrote the text, in English and Maguindanaon, and Bobby Timonera took the photographs. The Kadtuntaya Foundation published the 79-page book in 2008.
books.note: Published with the German Development Service (DED).
books.blurb: A photodocumentary of important actors in the Mindanao conflict, each narrating his/her vision of peace. Includes portraits of everyday life in rural North Cotabato and Maguindanao at the time of ceasefire: unstable yet filled with hope, awaiting the day that the Dar-ul Salam will not just be a vision, but a reality, for all war victims and perpetrators of this 41 year civil strife.

books.title: Galing ARMM!
books.subtitle: 8 Stories of Emerging Good Local Governance in a Misunderstood Land
books.summary: 8 case stories of good local governance from towns and provinces of the ARMM. It aims to counter the region's image as a place of failed government.
books.overview:
This book tells 8 stories of good local governance from the ARMM. Its subtitle, Emerging Good Local Governance in a Misunderstood Land, sets it against the region's image of violence and failed government. It was published in Quezon City by the Galing Pook Foundation, which since 1993 has recognised innovation and good practice in Philippine local government.

From 2010 the foundation also ran a separate Galing Pook Awards in ARMM, with the regional government and the Local Government Academy of the Department of the Interior and Local Government; its first round was funded by USAID through The Asia Foundation.

books.title: Mindanao
books.subtitle: A Gamble Worth Taking
books.summary: A Lowy Institute Paper on the prospects for peace in Mindanao and the threats to the GRP–MILF peace process. Written as foreign terrorists were using Mindanao as a haven, it argues that backing the peace process is a gamble worth taking.
books.overview:
Lowy Institute Paper 17 looks at the peace process between the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), at a time when Jemaah Islamiyah operatives linked to attacks across Southeast Asia, including both Bali bombings, were sheltering in Mindanao. It asks how foreign countries, among them Australia, the United States and Malaysia, can help.

The authors describe a conflict driven by a mix of clan ties, the greed of kidnap-for-ransom groups such as the Abu Sayyaf, real grievances of poor Moro farmers, and jihadist ideas. They warn that seeing it as a clash of 2 clear sides misses how clans sit in local government and in the insurgency at once. Their recommendations come as a package: stronger ceasefire monitoring and permanent peace panels, help for the MILF to become an unarmed political movement, quick and visible aid that also reaches Christian areas, and reform of the military.

Malcolm Cook led the Lowy Institute's Asia and Pacific programme. Kit Collier had written International Crisis Group reports on the Philippines. They argue that foreign support cannot guarantee peace, but that the gamble is worth taking.

books.title: Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, the Philippines
books.subtitle: Regional Election 2008: Report on the International Election Observation Mission, 4–13 August 2008
books.summary: The report of an international team that observed the August 2008 ARMM regional election. It records how the vote was run and the problems observers found.
books.overview:
The Asian Network for Free Elections (ANFREL), an Asian election-monitoring network, sent 22 observers to 6 provinces of the ARMM for the regional election of August 2008. This is the mission's report, written by Somsri Hananuntasuk and Ichal Supriadi with input from all the observers and dated November 2008. It was the first ARMM election run with automated voting and counting machines.

The observers called automation a welcome improvement over manual counting, and found the polls generally less violent than before. They also recorded serious problems: no voting booths to keep ballots secret, weak checks on voter identity that allowed underage and "phantom" voting in parts of Lanao del Sur and Maguindanao, election inspectors who openly favoured candidates, and widespread vote-buying. They praised the use of candidates' photographs to help voters identify them as an idea other countries could copy.

books.title: Journeying Together towards a Culture of Peace in Mindanao
books.subtitle: The Bishops-Ulama Forum, 1996–98: A Report of the First Two Years
books.summary: A report on the first 2 years of the Bishops-Ulama Forum, which brought Catholic bishops and Muslim religious leaders together after the 1996 peace agreement. It records their dialogues and joint work for Muslim–Christian peace.
books.overview:
This is a report from the Bishops-Ulama Forum. The forum was launched in Cebu City in November 1996 and brought together Catholic bishops and Muslim religious leaders from across Mindanao. Published in 1998, the report covers the forum's first 2 years, with its dialogues and joint work for peace between Muslims and Christians.

The forum held that the Mindanao conflict should not be seen as a religious war, and ran workshops on a culture of peace in local communities. From 1998 it also sponsored a yearly Mindanao Week of Peace.

books.title: Living Peace
books.subtitle: Stories of Hope & Collective Action towards Building a Culture of Peace in Mindanao
books.summary: Stories of communities in Mindanao working together to build peace after decades of conflict. It shows the peace and development work of the ACT for Peace programme on the ground.
books.overview: This book tells stories of Mindanao communities working together to build a culture of peace. It was written by Madonna T. Virola and Marides V. Virola and edited by Gail T. Ilagan, and runs to 146 illustrated pages. It was published in Davao City in 2009 by the ACT for Peace Programme, a joint programme of the Philippine government and the United Nations. The programme worked for human security and a culture of peace in communities hit by or at risk of conflict. Library records file the book under peacebuilding and peace movements in Mindanao, and the island's politics and social policy.

books.title: Journey to the Bangsamoro
books.summary: A 3-volume history of the GPH–MILF peace negotiations from the MILF side, with copies of every signed agreement between the 2 parties. Volume 1 covers the domestic phase of the talks from 1997 to 2000.
books.overview:
Journey to the Bangsamoro was published in 2015 by the MILF Peace Panel in 3 volumes. It tells the history of the peace negotiations between the government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, and reproduces every agreement the 2 sides signed.

The panel meant it to show stakeholders why the process matters historically, to record what it achieved, and to urge continued commitment to the process and its agreements. Volume 1 covers the domestic phase of the talks, from 1997 to 2000.
books.note: Published by the MILF Peace Panel.

books.title: The Bangsamoro People's Struggle against Oppression and Colonialism
books.summary: Writings by the founding chairman of the MILF on the Bangsamoro struggle against oppression and colonial rule. It sets out the MILF's case for Bangsamoro self-determination.
books.overview: Salamat Hashim (1939 to 2003) was the founder and leader of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front. This collection of his writings was published in 2001 by the MILF's Agency for Youth Affairs. It sets out the MILF's account of the Bangsamoro struggle against oppression and colonial rule, and its case for the Bangsamoro right to self-determination. It is listed among his works between a 1985 book on the Bangsamoro mujahid and a 2002 piece proposing a referendum as a peaceful way to settle the Mindanao conflict.
books.note: Published by the MILF’s Agency for Youth Affairs.

books.title: Bangsamoro and the Everyday
books.subtitle: Stories from the Heart of the Revolution
books.summary: A collection of personal stories from inside the Bangsamoro revolution, launched in Cotabato City on 17 June 2026. Its premise is to tell stories that had to stay hidden while the movement was clandestine.
books.overview:
Bangsamoro and the Everyday: Stories from the Heart of the Revolution gathers personal accounts from Bangsamoro men, women, youth, families, communities and members of the movement. They tell of life during the armed struggle, its cost, and the turn to peace. The Institute of Bangsamoro Studies and the Bangsamoro Government launched it at the Grand Pagana Hotel in Cotabato City on 17 June 2026.

It has 6 chapters. The first looks at the historical, intellectual and spiritual roots of the struggle. The second shows what the conflict did to individuals, families and children. The third tells the jihad as it was lived in the Ranaw region. The fourth looks inside the revolutionary fronts and how they spoke for the main sectors of society. The fifth follows the move from armed struggle to peace talks. The sixth records the doctors, lawyers, teachers, scholars and civil society groups who supported the cause.

One author, Bam Baraguir, said the project took nearly 5 years. She explained that every claim had to be grounded in the stories the team gathered, "to help us remember".

books.title: The Three Faces of Mindanao
books.subtitle: A Comparative Case Study of Three Communities in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao
books.summary: A comparison of 3 communities in the ARMM and how their history, autonomy and social conditions differ. It was published with Action Against Hunger and the European Commission.
books.overview:
This study compares 3 communities in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, looking at their history, the autonomy movement and social conditions. The research writers were Erlinda M. Burton, Cecilia Macabuac and Lourdes A. Wong of the Research Institute for Mindanao Culture at Xavier University in Cagayan de Oro. It was published around 2004 with Accion Contra el Hambre (Action Against Hunger) in Cotabato City and the European Commission, and runs to 123 pages with a short bibliography.

Burton, the first-named writer, was an anthropologist and archaeologist. She trained at Brigham Young University in Utah and took a doctorate in medical anthropology at the University of Pittsburgh in 1983, with a thesis on modern medicine among the Agusan Manobo. From Xavier she did field research across Mindanao for decades, much of it among indigenous communities, for clients from UNESCO to the Ford Foundation. She died in 2018.
books.note: Published with Action Against Hunger and the European Commission.

books.title: Human Rights Treatise on Women, Islam, and Democracy
books.summary: A study of the rights and legal status of Muslim women in Mindanao, set against Islam and Philippine democracy. It looks at women's rights in Islamic law and in Philippine practice.
books.overview: This 148-page study was published by the Ateneo Human Rights Center in 2004. Library records list its subjects as human rights and women's rights in Mindanao, the legal status of Muslim women in the Philippines, and women in Islam. It includes a bibliography.

books.title: Women and Conflict
books.subtitle: Trafficking in Persons in Internally Displaced People Camps in Mindanao
books.summary: A study of how displacement by armed conflict leaves people in Mindanao's evacuation camps open to human trafficking. It documents a problem long suspected but little studied.
books.overview:
This study by the Mindanao Migrants Center for Empowering Actions (MMCEAI), with Mary Fe Arquiza as author, looks at the link between displacement by armed conflict and human trafficking. It came out of action research funded by Oxfam in 2010 among people displaced by the 2008 fighting. The team visited evacuation camps in 7 ARMM municipalities and in Lanao del Sur and gathered accounts from 130 respondents. The research was prompted by reports of 2 children who went missing in 2008 after being recruited from camps in Kolambugan, Lanao del Norte.

It found that recruiters and traffickers moved into the camps posing as relief workers and offering jobs, often abroad, and that the first weeks in a camp were the most dangerous. Some recruits agreed to false travel documents to be sent out faster. The first recommendation is to end the war. Others include social protection, cash aid, legal and trauma support for victims, better shelters, and teaching evacuees about illegal recruitment.
